items.title: 'Panicked' Putin has big decision to make, and 'could go nuclear'
items.description: The Russian president's decision to annex Crimea showed the world his authoritarian muscle. These days, it is a "personal humiliation".

items.title: Widow warns of shock ambulance bill after husband's unexpected death
items.description: Private health insurers can legally avoid ambulance bills because corpses are not considered patients, a loophole that left a grieving widow shocked.

items.title: Suspected bird flu cases detected in NSW and WA after devastating impact overseas
items.description: A suspected positive case of H5 bird flu has been identified in New South Wales, the state agriculture minister has announced.

items.title: West Coast star Adam Hunter's 'grieving best mate' slams AFL leadership
items.description: In a five-page letter to the executives and commissioners of the AFL, a grieving best mate has slammed the organisation for "failing" former West Coasts player Adam Hunter, who suffered from CTE.

items.title: For decades Australian house prices have grown. This is what a fall could mean
items.description: After decades of growth, Australian house prices are slowing. Here's what a fall could look like.

items.title: Man who spent eight days stuck under collapsed shopping centre in Venezuela rescued alive
items.description: Hernan Alberto Gil Flores, a 43-year-old Venezuelan man was dug out alive from under the ruins of a collapsed shopping centre, eight days after devastating earthquakes shook the nation.

items.title: Meeting to decide Moira Deeming's future cancelled amid court battle
items.description: Victorian MP Moira Deeming has won a two-week reprieve as a Liberal candidate for the November state election, after the party agreed in the Supreme Court to cancel imminent plans to revoke her preselection.

items.title: Breaking: Woman who attacked Senator Lidia Thorpe outside the MCG avoids jail
items.description: Lidia Thorpe was with a group of friends near the stadium after the Dreamtime at the G game between Essendon and Richmond when she was attacked by Ebony Jan Bell.

items.title: Pub for breakfast: How World Cup watch parties took over Australia
items.description: They were just supposed to be somewhere to watch the match, but World Cup viewing parties have ended up becoming so much more.

items.title: Photos show site of US pilot's killing at hands of Papua rebels
items.description: A Papua separatist group has shot dead an American pilot who allegedly transported Indonesian troops into the restive province.

items.title: 'Advocate for yourself': Woman's warning after partner's cancer death
items.description: Rory Esler's family and friends will take part in the Gold Coast marathon festival this weekend to honour his memory and to raise awareness, encouraging young Australians to advocate for themselves when navigating the medical system.

items.title: Worst start to ski season since 1957, as blizzard finally dumps snow
items.description: Following the worst start to a ski season in decades, a major snowstorm hit the NSW and Victorian Alps last night.

items.title: Ohio town in shock after 16 kids found in squalor 'right under our noses'
items.description: Just days after authorities removed 16 children from a squalid home and arrested four adult relatives, the question looms over their southern Ohio village: how could this have happened, for years, unnoticed?

items.title: Gary Glitter charged with historical child sex offences
items.description: The charges were linked to alleged sexual offences against a child dating back to 1978, British prosecutors said.

items.title: How to keep your home warm if you're renting or on a budget
items.description: If you're searching for ways to make your home warmer, these easy and inexpensive tricks can make a big difference.

items.title: 'Deadly' Indigenous remote artists travel to Sydney
items.description: Remote Indigenous artists from around Australia are in Sydney for the annual National Indigenous Art Fair.

items.title: Hearing is believing as national braille music camp celebrates 40 years
items.description: Four decades ago, 92-year-old Roma Dix co-founded a braille music camp for visually impaired children. This week they're celebrating its 40th anniversary in full song.

items.title: Can the Socceroos beat Egypt?
items.description: Can the Socceroos beat Egypt and win their first ever knockout final at a World Cup?  The Pharaohs have Salah, Marmoush and a dangerous counterattack, but the Socceroos have the physical edge, aerial threats and set-piece power to cause serious problems. We take a closer look Egypt's strengths, and why Australia are a dangerous underdog that shouldn't be written off.

items.title: Australian in Israeli Defence Force committed war crimes, report alleges
items.description: The Australian Federal Police are considering a brief of evidence from the Australian Centre for International Justice, detailing alleged war crimes in Gaza by an Australian citizen who was in the Israeli Defence Force.

items.title: Secret police recordings of croc wrangler Matt Wright released
items.description: Secretly recorded phone calls and conversations crucial to the criminal case against celebrity crocodile wrangler Matt Wright during his Northern Territory Supreme Court trial have been released to the media.

items.title: Why would Taylor Swift get married at Madison Square Garden?
items.description: Fans believe they know the when and where of Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce's upcoming nuptials, but much of the reported two-day extravaganza will likely be a cloak-and-dagger operation.

items.title: Live: ASX on the up, PEXA shares lose 20pc in value
items.description: The ASX has risen strongly after weaker US jobs data eased interest rate hike expectations. PEXA shares have lost 20 per cent in value after an IPART draft report recommended cutting PEXA regulated revenue. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Kyiv suffers deadliest attack this year, after Russia 'unleashed hell'
items.description: At least 27 people are dead and the city's key Red Cross warehouse has been destroyed, as search efforts are still underway.

items.title: University's chancellor quits as ICAC inquiry continues
items.description: UOW Chancellor Michael Still resigns as the state's corruption watchdog continues to investigate allegations of improper governance, recruitment decisions and consultancy engagements.

items.title: Jewish community frustrated by delays to social media duty of care
items.description: A mandated digital duty of care for social media platforms remains more than 18 months away, despite an online safety law review recommending its implementation in 2024.
